database_summary: Small analytical OLTP/data-mart style SQLite database for a beverage/retail domain. It contains master/dimension tables for products, packaging, customers, breweries, locations, employees, and some time-series/measurement tables for monthly sales, purchases, inventory, web metrics and logs. Many tables are descriptive (dimensions/entities) and several are event/measurement/history tables (monthly_sales, purchases, web_page_visits, web_counter_hist, ticker, server_heartbeat, picking_log). Foreign keys are declared but some composite primary keys are modeled as multiple PK columns. Care is required joining tables with one-to-many relationships (e.g., products -> monthly_sales -> purchases -> inventory -> orderlines) because joins can multiply rows.

accepted.name: product_monthly_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  mth,
  qty
FROM
  monthly_sales
accepted.description: Monthly aggregated sales per product (one row per product_id + mth) exposing qty and running totals useful for trend analysis, comparisons to budget, and time series joins with product attributes. | Use for: time series of sales for a product; compare actual monthly sales to budget; aggregate sales by product group after joining products/product_groups; compute growth rates month-over-month

accepted.name: product_monthly_sales_with_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ms.product_id,
  ms.mth,
  ms.qty,
  p.id AS id,
  p.name AS name,
  p.group_id AS group_id,
  pg.id AS id,
  pg.name AS name
FROM
  monthly_sales ms
  LEFT JOIN products p ON ms.product_id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON p.group_id = pg.id
accepted.description: Monthly sales per product enriched with product and product group attributes. Useful when questions need product names, group names, or to filter/aggregate by group. | Use for: list top-selling products by month with product names; compare sales across product groups; filter monthly sales for specific product attributes

accepted.name: purchases_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id,
  p.purchased,
  p.brewery_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.qty,
  p.cost,
  b.id AS id,
  b.name AS name,
  prod.id AS id,
  prod.name AS name,
  prod.group_id AS group_id
FROM
  purchases p
  LEFT JOIN breweries b ON p.brewery_id = b.id
  LEFT JOIN products prod ON p.product_id = prod.id
accepted.description: Purchase transactions enriched with product and brewery attributes. One row per purchase transaction (id). Useful for cost analysis, supplier performance, and joining to inventory/purchases timelines. | Use for: total cost by brewery or product over a period; match purchases to inventory receipts; supplier analysis: average cost per product from each brewery

accepted.name: inventory_stock_by_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  location_id,
  SUM(qty) AS qty_on_hand
FROM
  inventory
GROUP BY
  product_id,
  location_id
accepted.description: Current inventory stock quantities aggregated by product and location. One row per product_id + location_id exposing total qty on hand. Useful for replenishment, location-level stock checks, and joining to locations or products. | Use for: how much stock of a product exists at a location; identify products below minimums when joined to product_minimums; prepare pick lists by available qty at locations

accepted.name: orders_with_lines_and_customers
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.id AS id,
  ol.order_id,
  ol.product_id,
  ol.qty,
  ol.amount,
  o.id AS id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.ordered,
  o.delivery,
  c.id AS id,
  c.name AS name
FROM
  orderlines ol
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
accepted.description: Orders denormalized with their orderlines and customer attributes. One row per orderline (id from orderlines) to support revenue, order-level and customer-level analytics. | Use for: compute revenue per order or customer; list orderlines with customer names for fulfilment; analyze order lead times between ordered and delivery

accepted.name: web_daily_device_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  pc,
  tablet,
  phone,
  (IFNULL(pc,0) + IFNULL(tablet,0) + IFNULL(phone,0)) AS total
FROM
  web_devices
accepted.description: Daily web device counts with a total visits measure. One row per day; normalizes device columns and provides a derived total measure for easy trend/ratio calculations. | Use for: device mix over time; percentage of traffic from mobile vs desktop; join with web_demographics by day

accepted.name: web_demographics_unpivot
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT day, 'M' AS letter, 'tw' AS channel_shortcut, m_tw_cnt AS cnt, m_tw_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'M' AS letter, 'fb' AS channel_shortcut, m_fb_cnt AS cnt, m_fb_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS letter, 'tw' AS channel_shortcut, f_tw_cnt AS cnt, f_tw_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS letter, 'fb' AS channel_shortcut, f_fb_cnt AS cnt, f_fb_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
accepted.description: Unpivots the pre-aggregated web_demographics row into rows per day x gender x channel with counts and qty. One row per day+gender+channel exposing cnt and qty, enabling segmentation queries across genders and channels. | Use for: compare counts/qty across channels and genders; join with gender_dim or channels_dim by letter or shortcut; compute share of channel by gender and vice versa

accepted.name: latest_ticker_per_symbol
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  symbol,
  day,
  price,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY day DESC) AS rn
FROM
  ticker
accepted.description: Latest ticker price per stock symbol using a window rank by day. One row per symbol+day with rank, enabling downstream filtering for the most recent price per symbol (WHERE rn = 1). | Use for: get latest price per stock symbol; time series of ticker with ability to pick top N recent days; merge latest price to stock master
